items.question: How does client-side image compression work without server uploads?
items.answer: Images are drawn to an HTML5 Canvas using createImageBitmap and re-encoded directly in browser memory at your designated quality setting. Zero bytes are uploaded to any server.

items.question: Are EXIF metadata and GPS locations stripped during compression?
items.answer: Yes. Drawing an image to a canvas naturally strips all EXIF metadata, camera settings, and geolocation tags, enhancing privacy while reducing file weight.

items.question: What happens if the compressed result is larger than the original?
items.answer: If re-encoding does not yield a smaller file size (common when attempting to re-compress already heavily optimized files), the tool automatically preserves your original file and alerts you.

items.question: Which image formats are supported for compression?
items.answer: JPEG, WebP, and PNG images are supported. You can re-encode JPEGs and WebPs with custom quality factors or convert PNGs to modern WebP.

items.question: Can I compress multiple images at once?
items.answer: Yes. You can drag and drop multiple files to compress them simultaneously and download them individually or as a ZIP archive.

items.question: What quality setting offers the best balance of file size and visual fidelity?
items.answer: A quality factor between 0.70 and 0.80 typically reduces JPEG and WebP file weight by 60% to 80% with virtually imperceptible visual compression artifacts on web screens.

items.question: Why should I set a maximum pixel dimension?
items.answer: Modern smartphone cameras capture images at 4000+ pixels wide. Constraining resolution to 1920 or 2048 pixels yields dramatic file size reductions before compression even begins.

items.question: Can this tool process high-resolution DSLR photos safely?
items.answer: Yes. The engine uses createImageBitmap and automatically revokes object URLs upon completion, ensuring browser memory is freed immediately.
